coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–7 miles, Z2 only (130–140 bpm ceiling), 300–400 ft vert if terrain allows. You're 8 days out and your RHR is at 51—that's excellent taper signal. Your last three runs sit at 128–129 bpm, which is solidly aerobic, so keep Thursday loose and short. This isn't a fitness day; it's active recovery and CNS downregulation. Run by feel, no watch obsessing. If you're in transit for work today, a hotel treadmill at easy pace counts—don't skip it chasing perfect terrain.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You slept 8.63 hours at 92.6% efficiency—use that recovery momentum. Eat 1.2–1.5g carbs per kg bodyweight today spread across 4–5 meals; your glycogen is fully topped from an easy week. Focus on anti-inflammatory foods: fatty fish, berries, leafy greens, turmeric. Skip any processed inflammatory markers. Hydrate to pale urine; alpine terrain and constant work travel can dehydrate you faster than you notice. If flying or moving between time zones today, add 500 mL electrolyte drink (sodium ~500–600mg per liter) to counteract travel sweat and cabin dehydration.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Your recovery score of 96/100 and 51 bpm resting heart rate say you're prepared for race week. Maintain 8+ hours of sleep nightly through race day—this is non-negotiable for alpine 50K performance where fatigue and altitude interact. You've got no HRV data, so rely on that RHR trend: if it creeps above 60 in the next 8 days, dial back intensity immediately. Cold-water immersion or ice baths are off the table now; use 10–15 min easy foam rolling on quads, calves, IT band instead. Compression sleeves optional but not essential at this recovery score.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're in the taper sweet spot: fitness is locked in, body is recovered, and doubt creeps in. Expect it. Reframe the next 8 days as sharpening the tool, not building it. Review your Julian Alps 50K course map—study the aid station locations, the descent profiles (where you'll make time), the exposed ridge sections (wind, exposure management). Visualize 2–3 key race moments: the 20-mile wall, your strongest climb, your target finish pace. This mental work calms the noise and gives you tactical specificity alpine terrain demands. You've put in the work; trust it.
